key_insight: Using deployment-specific context (such as provider type, department, and model used) improves prediction of whether clinicians will reject an LLM response.
clinical_relevance: A pre-response rejection-risk model could help clinical LLM systems trigger guardrails or abstain selectively, potentially improving trust and practical usefulness in real-world EHR workflows.
method: Trained a pre-response classifier on query content plus deployment context available before generation.
Evaluated the model prospectively on sparse user feedback from a clinical LLM embedded in an electronic health record system.
Estimated downstream impact for two uses: guardrail triggering and abstention.
evidence_signal: In a 4.5-month prospective analysis, the prediction model achieved an AUROC of 0.719.
watch_item: Because feedback is sparse and deployment-specific, performance may not generalize cleanly across hospitals, workflows, or model versions without recalibration.
paper_title: Deployment-Centered Evaluation: Predicting Query-Level Rejection Risk in a Clinical LLM System
